Maria —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. We're keen to get this closed quickly. High-level position from our side to start the conversation:

- Liability cap: Redwood's standard is that aggregate liability is capped at the greater of (i) total fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim or (ii) an amount agreed in the Order Form. We are open to targeted carve-outs for third-party IP claims, but we generally require either (a) that Redwood received same‑day indemnities from upstream vendors or (b) the customer accepts a pass‑through only where Redwood has no contractual recourse against the upstream provider.

- Consequential damages: we maintain the general exclusion; we can agree a limited carve‑out for data breach where Redwood's gross negligence is proven, subject to a negotiated cap tied to the affected product fees.

- Models & licensing: we treat claims arising from third‑party licensed model components similarly to OSS components, but we need specificity: which artifacts in the Order Form are considered "third‑party" (models, weights, adapters, etc.).

Subject: Proposed redlines — Third‑party IP pass‑through and model license language

Maria / Karthik,

Thanks — drafted two short alternatives below to help move the discussion. These are high‑level snippets, not final MSA text, but should make the tradeoffs clear. I attached a tracked version with our suggested edits: MSA_redlines_May2026.docx

ALTERNATIVE A (LIMITED PASS‑THROUGH)
If Redwood receives written notice that a claim of third‑party intellectual property infringement arises solely from pre‑existing third‑party open source software or third‑party model components provided by Redwood: (i) Redwood shall, at its option, (a) obtain a license for Customer's continued use, (b) replace or modify the infringing component, or (c) if neither option is commercially feasible, accept liability for direct damages caused solely by such claim. Redwood's liability under this section shall not exceed the greater of (1) fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim or (2) USD 500,000; provided, however, that this section shall not apply where Redwood has a contractually‑enforceable indemnity from the upstream supplier for the same claim.

ALTERNATIVE B (CUSTOMER‑BACKED UNLIMITED PASS‑THROUGH)
Customer may elect to treat third‑party open source and third‑party model component infringement claims as pass‑through (i.e., not subject to Redwood's liability cap) by executing an addendum to the Order Form whereby Customer agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Redwood for any downstream claims that exceed Redwood's actual damages for the claim. This option requires disclosure of the specific third‑party components at time of Order Form execution and a technical attestation of versioning.

NOTES / QUESTIONS
- We treat "models" as deliverables; we need DataScale to identify whether you expect Redwood to support third‑party supplied model weights or only Redwood‑hosted model variants.
- We are reluctant to accept an uncapped pass‑through without either: (a) upstream indemnity, or (b) customer indemnity that covers third‑party upstream liability.
- Consequential damages carve‑out for gross negligence on data breach: we can agree to this with a narrow cap and a requirement of demonstrable harm (for example, direct incident response and notification costs).

If DataScale prefers, we can mark up your redline directly with ALTERNATIVE A as our suggested path forward; ALTERNATIVE B can be used if you require uncapped pass‑through but are willing to reciprocate via indemnity.

Available for a 30‑minute call Thursday AM.
